  Readable gloss: "This Hebrew noun captures the insidious power of destructive speech -- from quiet whispering behind someone's back to a full-blown defamatory report. In Genesis 37:2, young Joseph brings back a 'bad report' about his brothers, setting in motion the drama of jealousy and exile. The spies who discouraged Israel from entering Canaan spread a dibbah of the land (Num 13:32; 14:36-37), and Jeremiah heard the dibbah of many whispering against him (Jer 20:10). The word conveys speech that glides stealthily, undermining trust and inciting harm."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: "slander, evil report, defamation"
    Enriched: Whispering, slander, defamation, or an evil report -- malicious speech designed to damage someone's standing or discourage action. Spanish translations use 'calumnia' and 'difamacion,' capturing the defamatory force, while French employs 'calomnie.' The semantic range spans from private malicious gossip (Ps 31:13; Jer 20:10) to the public spreading of a damaging report (Gen 37:2; Num 13:32). Prove...
    Existing Spanish translations: calumnia-de, difamación, infame-de, infamia, infamia-de-, informe-de-ellos, murmurar-de, y-murmullo-de, y-tu-difamación

    "1": { "label": "Short Spanish label for sense 1", "enriched": "Translated enriched description for sense 1 in Spanish" },
    "2": { "label": "...", "enriched": "..." }
  }
}

- Translate naturally into Spanish, not word-for-word. Adapt idioms and tone.
